finding: Mortgage pricing includes Treasury cash-flow structure, prepayment option and origination/servicing margins. Expectations of future policy rates influence long yields. Spread exceeded300bp in2007-09; not stable through crises.
methodology: Paul Willen Current Policy Perspectives26-3; author analysis, not official FOMC view. No single ten-year duration applies to every MBS.

finding: Current historical series support an approximately1.7pp long-run spread and episodic>3pp widening, with2.01pp onJune18,2026.
methodology: Freddie Mac weekly PMMS versus Fed H15 daily10yr CMT; independent same-release-date subtraction has timing mismatch. Historical observations available then; exact upload-vintage revision state not recovered. Download supplied two CSVs insideZIP.

finding: Pre-upload weekly30yr FRM6.47%,15yr5.81%; supports around6.5%, not an individual offer.
methodology: Conventional conforming fully amortizing purchase applications,20%down,excellent credit; national weekly mean note rate, not APR or every mortgage.

finding: Fixed coupons and market yield-to-maturity are different. Auctions determine new-issue yield/price; secondary-market yields change with price.

methodology: Statement establishes policy announcement, not completed purchase volume or causal rate effect; its sub6% assertion uses an unspecified measure unlikePMMS.

methodology: ACM statistical model; estimates depend on model and vintage. No exact upload-day numerical model download recovered.

finding: HELOCs commonly have a variable indexed rate plus margin. A second lien may preserve the first mortgage while adding debt and payment risk.

finding: The weekly Freddie Mac benchmark peaked at 18.63% on October 9, 1981; roughly 3% in 2021 is supported.
methodology: Current historical mirror; no inflation-adjusted house-price or wage comparison inferred.

finding: MBS commonly come from Ginnie Mae, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, with different guarantee structures. Private-label MBS also exist; prepayments create reinvestment risk.
methodology: Current official product guidance, no precise upload-era market share or universal underwriting-quality claim certified.

finding: Credit cards and small-business loans often reference prime, which banks partly base on the federal funds target.
methodology: Contractual short-rate benchmarks are not the ten-year Treasury; current guidance vintage only.

finding: Fixed-rate principal and interest can stay constant while taxes and insurance change the total monthly payment.
methodology: Dated consumer publication for standard fully amortizing mortgages.

finding: Refinancing depends on costs, holding period, credit, income, equity and loan term. A borrower may not qualify.
methodology: Last update August 27, 2008; historical financial mechanics only, not current disclosure-law guidance. Break-even is net cost divided by monthly savings.

finding: MOVE measures option-implied Treasury-yield volatility; volatility is not a prediction of direction.
methodology: Issuer release; the transcript does not name MOVE, so identifying the unnamed fear gauge as MOVE is an analyst inference.
